transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can go back to light exercise after 1 week, and that includes gardening.  
Just avoid heavy lifting or strenuous work for a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If you were using eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise.  
If you’re running low, your GP should be able to provide more.

Any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
A bit of light sensitivity can be normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses.  
If it’s mild and things just seem brighter, wear sunglasses when you go outside.

But severe light sensitivity, especially if the eye is red and painful, is not normal and may need checking.

Any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It’s common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after your operation.  
It should improve quickly and settle down over time. If it’s still blurry, or getting worse, we may need to check it.

Any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't have any more questions. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you feel that all your questions have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. Thank you for addressing all my concerns!

verdict.label: pass
